theory: A CAS session is an ordered log of cells admitted into one live segment, with the live namespace reconstructed from accepted cells. Reproduction compares captured output and available state fingerprints, and export separately checks both a fresh replay and the actual script a reader will execute.
instead_of: Treat a successful interpreter exit or matching stdout as proof of reproducibility; silent state changes and truncated output make that reading insufficient.

absorption.rationale: New languages using the existing framing shapes fit named backends; a third wire protocol reaches into the session extractor and retention accounting, rather than remaining an isolated adapter addition.

world_mapping.rationale: CellRecord, CellOutcome, segments, backend identity, and state-unchecked reports map directly to what was run and what was compared.

abstraction.rationale: Backend rendering, kernel lifetime, session admission, and fresh replay are separately named operations; a replay consumes the same recorded cells and explicit budget.

justification.rationale: The code explains the previously invisible failures: random state that prints nothing, failed cells mutating state, and shutdown markers that do not establish script completion.

honest_limits.rationale: Missing fingerprints and clipped captures are explicitly unverified, and replay budgets leave unreached cells as None instead of manufacturing outcomes.

rehearsals.requirement: Add another command-line CAS with sentinel framing.
rehearsals.why: A backend supplies language rendering and framing details and is registered in BACKENDS.

rehearsals.requirement: Report replay of an old log that never recorded namespace fingerprints.
rehearsals.why: The existing state_unchecked and digestless reporting preserve the distinction between output agreement and state verification.

rehearsals.requirement: Support a persistent kernel whose replies arrive over a different message protocol.
rehearsals.why: Session framing selection and capture-size arithmetic currently distinguish length and sentinel protocols directly.
